sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Climate Change** refers to long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns.
**Global Warming** driven by **Greenhouse Gases (GHGs)** like CO2, CH4, and N2O.
**Kyoto Protocol (1997)** focused on binding emission reduction targets.
**Paris Agreement (2015)** aims to limit global warming to well below **2°C**.
Variety of life on Earth; threatened by **habitat loss** and **pollution**.
Sustainable management of natural resources to prevent **extinction**.
Introduction of harmful contaminants into the environment (Air, Water, Soil).
Questions on **Environmental Acts**, **International Summits**, and **National Parks**.
Essential for **General Awareness** section in UPSSSC PET exam.

items.title: Greenhouse Gases (GHGs) - Mnemonic: 'CO-M-N-O-W'
items.content:
• **CO2**: Carbon Dioxide (Primary contributor)
• **M**: Methane (CH4)
• **N**: Nitrous Oxide (N2O)
• **O**: Ozone (O3)
• **W**: Water Vapor
• **Mnemonic:** 'CO-M-N-O-W' (Come Now, Open Window) to remember the major GHGs.

items.title: Major Environmental Acts in India
items.content:
• **Wildlife Protection Act**: 1972
• **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act**: 1974
• **Forest (Conservation) Act**: 1980
• **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act**: 1981
• **Environment (Protection) Act**: 1986

items.title: Biodiversity Hotspots - Mnemonic: 'H-I-W-S'
items.content:
• **H**: Himalayas
• **I**: Indo-Burma region
• **W**: Western Ghats
• **S**: Sundaland
• **Mnemonic:** 'HI-WS' (High-Ways) to remember the 4 biodiversity hotspots in India.

items.title: Global Summits Timeline
items.content:
• **Stockholm Conference**: 1972 (First major UN conference on environment)
• **Earth Summit (Rio)**: 1992 (Agenda 21)
• **Kyoto Protocol**: 1997 (Emission targets)
• **Paris Agreement**: 2015 (Climate goal)

items.title: Pollution Types & Indicators
items.content:
• **Air Pollution**: Particulate Matter (PM 2.5, PM 10)
• **Water Pollution**: BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) as an indicator
• **Soil Pollution**: Pesticides and heavy metals
• **Noise Pollution**: Measured in Decibels (dB)

items.definition: Remember **1972** (Wildlife Act), **1980** (Forest Act), **1986** (Environment Act) as a sequence of environmental legislation.
Ozone is in the **Stratosphere** (S for Stratosphere, S for Shield).
Remember **Methane (CH4)** is 25-30 times more potent than **CO2** in trapping heat.
Stockholm (1972) was the first; Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit. Do not confuse the two.
Kyoto (1997) is for emission targets; Paris (2015) is for temperature limits (2°C).
Montreal Protocol is for **Ozone depletion**; Kyoto/Paris are for **Global Warming**.
The gradual increase in Earth's average temperature due to **Greenhouse Effect**.
Caused primarily by **CFCs** (Chlorofluorocarbons) used in refrigerators and ACs.
The variety of flora and fauna in a particular habitat; essential for **ecosystem stability**.
Meeting present needs without compromising the ability of **future generations**.
The total amount of **GHGs** emitted by an individual, event, or organization.

upscNotes.content: Focus heavily on the years of Indian Environmental Acts as UPSSSC frequently asks for chronological order.
Memorize the headquarters of major organizations like UNEP (Nairobi) and IPCC (Geneva).
Students often confuse the Montreal Protocol (Ozone) with the Kyoto Protocol (Climate Change).
Do not ignore the 'Environment' section; it carries 2-3 marks in the General Awareness section.

keyTakeaways: Environment Protection Act was passed in 1986.
June 5 is celebrated as World Environment Day.
Methane is a major contributor to global warming.
Western Ghats is a recognized biodiversity hotspot.
The Paris Agreement aims to limit warming to 2°C.
